Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Kharif 2025, certified seed availability is 178.64 lakh quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level (ETL) and no major pest incidence was recorded. DPPQS was instructed to keep a close watch on Soyabean and Cotton crops through regular surveys in close coordination with other stakeholders. 7. Rainfall Forecast: - Overall, above normal rainfall activity is likely over most parts of central India; normal to above normal over many parts of northwest India including Western Himalayan Region: near normal over most parts of east & northeast India and below normal over south Peninsular India during the week. Advance of Southwest Monsoon: - The Southwest Monsoon has covered the entire country on 29th June, 2025, against the normal date of 08th July. - The Southwest Monsoon has further advanced into remaining parts of Rajasthan, West Uttar Pradesh and Haryana and entire Delhi today, the 29th June 2025. Thus, it has covered the entire country on 29th June, 2025, against the normal date of 08th July (9 days before the normal date of covering the entire India).
| 4 - The monsoon trough at mean sea level passes through Firozpur, Sonipat, Ayodhya, Gaya, Purulia, centre of the low-pressure area over Northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal and Bangladesh coasts and thence southeast wards to northeast Bay of Bengal.

chunks.heading: 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX
chunks.text:
| 5 Temerature Week 1 (27 June – 03 July2025): - Maximum temperatures are likely to be below normal by 2-4°C, over most parts of the country except northeast India, where it is likely to be above normal by 2- 3°C. Week 2 (04 July - 10 July 2025): - No significant change in maximum temperatures is likely as compared to week 1. These are likely to be below normal (1-3°C) or near normal over most parts of the country outside northeast India, where it is likely to be above normal by 2- 3°C.

chunks.heading: 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION
chunks.text:
Soil Moisture Observation - Soil moisture as on 27 June 2025 was similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in Gujarat, Rajasthan, M.P, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Haryana, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Jharkhand, Western and Bundelkhand regions of U.P. and Southern West Bengal. - It was lower than average of past 9 years in Northern parts of Bihar, Eastern U.P., Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Southern parts of Karnataka and N.E. Regions. | 7


Kharif Crops - Area coverage - Sugarcane: About 55.16 lakh ha area coverage under Sugarcane has been reported as compared to 54.88 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Cotton: About 54.66 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 59.97 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Jute: There has been a decline in area sown under Jute on account of diversion towards Maize and Sesamum.
